subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Assam: Bold and Malty
description: A micro-lesson that makes Assam: Bold and Malty usable.

hook.text: Assam is the world's largest tea-growing region. It sits in northeastern India's hot, humid Brahmaputra valley.

buildup.text: Assam uses the large-leafed assamica variety. Hot lowland conditions produce bold, full-bodied tea.

discovery.text: The characteristic malty, brisk character makes Assam the backbone of most English Breakfast blends.

twist.text: Assam's second flush (June) is the most prized. Monsoon rains followed by sun create peak flavor conditions.

climax.text: Over 800 tea estates operate in Assam, employing over a million workers. It's an economic powerhouse.

punchline.text: Bold, malty, essential. Assam is in almost every blend you drink.

quiz.question: What flavor characteristic makes Assam tea distinctive?

details.summary: Assam in northeastern India produces the world's most consumed black tea, prized for its bold, malty, and full-bodied character. Grown in hot, humid lowlands along the Brahmaputra River, Assam tea forms the backbone of breakfast blends like English Breakfast and Irish Breakfast worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Assam tea powers the global tea industry. Its robust flavor survives milk and sugar, making it the foundation of how most of the world drinks tea.
takeaways: Assam produces bold, malty black tea from assamica bushes
It is the base of most breakfast tea blends globally
Second flush in summer yields the prized tippy golden teas

faq.question: What is second flush Assam tea?
faq.answer: Second flush is harvested in June and July, producing leaves with golden tips and the richest, most muscatel flavor. This flush is the most prized and expensive Assam tea. First flush in spring is lighter and more floral, while rain teas later in the year are bold but simple.

faq.question: Why is Assam tea so strong compared to other teas?
faq.answer: Assam uses the large-leaved assamica variety, which contains more tannins and gives a robust, full-bodied cup. The hot, humid growing conditions produce rapid leaf growth with bold flavor compounds. CTC processing further intensifies the brew strength for a powerful cup.
